reports.title: PPL Corporation Delivers Strong Third-Quarter 2026 Earnings;

lines: •Narrows 2026 ongoing earnings forecast range to $1.92 to $1.96 per share; on track to achieve at least the midpoint of $1.94 per share.

•Increases long-term annual EPS growth target to 7% to 9% through at least 2030 off of the company’s 2026 ongoing earnings forecast midpoint; expects annual EPS growth in the top half of the targeted range.
•Provides 2027 earnings forecast range of $2.06 to $2.14 per share; midpoint of $2.10 per share represents an 8.2% increase over PPL’s projected 2026 ongoing earnings midpoint.

“Our strong third-quarter results reflect continued execution across PPL and keep us on track to meet or exceed the $1.94 per share midpoint of our 2026 ongoing earnings forecast range,” said Vincent Sorgi, PPL President and Chief Executive Officer.

With PPL’s updated business plan, the company increased its annual EPS growth target to 7% to 9% through at least 2030 off of the company’s 2026 ongoing earnings forecast midpoint, with annual growth expected in the top half of the range.
In conjunction with today’s business plan update, PPL provided a 2027 earnings forecast range of $2.06 to $2.14 per share.

desk.headline: Ongoing EPS up 13% to $0.54, slight beat; 2026 range narrowed, 2027 set at $2.06–2.14 and growth target lifted
results: Revenue rose 12% to $2.5bn; ongoing EPS climbed to $0.54 from $0.48 and reported EPS to $0.49 from $0.43.
Kentucky (+$0.04 a share) gained from new rates from January and higher sales; Pennsylvania (+$0.04) from new distribution rates from July and transmission investment.
Corporate costs weighed $0.02 a share more, mainly higher interest; special items, largely Rhode Island integration costs, cost $0.05 a share.
Nine-month operating cash flow was $2.06bn against $3.53bn of capital spending; long-term debt rose to $19.9bn.
Data centre pipeline kept growing: about 35.3 GW in advanced planning in Pennsylvania and 14.7 GW of economic development load in Kentucky.

guidance.summary: PPL tightened its 2026 ongoing EPS range around an unchanged $1.94 midpoint, gave a first 2027 range of $2.06–2.14, and raised its yearly EPS growth target to 7–9% through at least 2030 (was 6–8%).

points: Management presented the higher growth target as a base plan rather than a stretch, with the bigger capital plan driving about 10% yearly rate base growth.
It stressed that large new customers such as data centres should carry the cost of the grid they need, framed as 'growth pays for growth'.
On the roughly 2 GW Invitium deal with QTS, it said a binding agreement is still to come but voiced no concern about getting there.
About $3bn of new equity is planned through 2030, mostly via at-the-market sales; dividend growth to sit at the low end of 4–6%.
Regulatory setbacks noted: Kentucky did not approve a mechanism to delay rate cases, so new filings are expected, and Rhode Island granted only part of its rate request.
